title: Machine learning on phone and satellite data targets emergency aid in Togo
summary: Machine learning trained on survey consumption and wealth measures recognized poverty patterns in satellite and mobile phone data and was used to determine eligibility for Togo's Novissi COVID-19 cash transfer program. Compared with alternative targeting regimes, it reduced exclusion errors by 4-21% relative to geographic targeting and by 9-35% relative to a hypothetical social registry. Comparisons are counterfactual and the model types are not named in the abstract; this is a version 1 SSRN working paper.
ai_technology: Machine learning algorithms trained on survey-based poverty measures to score satellite and mobile phone network data

evidence.tested: Comparison with survey ground truth for the deployed program under alternative targeting regimes.
evidence.unknown: Model types, long-run outcomes and transfer to other countries; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Ranks regions and mobile subscribers by predicted poverty to prioritize aid.
